about: Paztport version 4 over HTTP: conformance vectors. The keys, the `mesh` and `ops` policies and their proofs are the ones in v4.json, by name; only the `payment` key is new, derived by v4.json's rule (seed = SHA-256(utf8("paztport-v3-vector-key:payment")), the same PKCS#8 and SPKI encodings, both base64url), and the boundary key below is SHA-256(utf8("paztport-http-v3-vector-boundary-key")), base64url. The v3 in these seed strings is historical: they are http-v3.json's, kept so that the keys, resultHash, requestBinding, boundaryInfluence, and operations but for `receive`, are http-v3.json's value for value, and headerNames holds each of http-v3.json's cases. resultHash maps a status and body (hex) to the result hash. requestBinding maps a method, a target (the raw path plus `?` and the raw query when there is one) and a body (hex) to the request binding. headerNames maps a header name to whether it is Paztport's: it begins with `X-Path-`, compared case-insensitively over ASCII. A responses case is a request chain `sent` from gateway to orders to payment, with the blocks `sentBlocks` sent beside it, one per stamp, and the `responseHeader` payment returned; the caller `orders` checks it against `status` and `body` (hex) with the proof the policy named holds for `proofRoute`, as a verifier that acts on the extensions in `actsOn` and carries the names in `allowedExtensions` (null for unset, which carries any name), whose policy window ends at `policyNotAfter` and whose clock reads `now`, running the check `uses` times against one nonce cache of nonceTtlMs that already holds `spent` (none when absent), each nonce key the JCS text of its array of strings. It expects the last result, {reason, suspectSvc, suspectInst, handOver, resultHash}: handOver is null unless the reason is OK, and then has one member per name in actsOn, each an array of {svc, items}, one per stamp of the sent chain and then the response stamp, items null where the stamp's block does not name the extension, as v4.json's verify cases record it. The responses cases on the `ops` policy run on a chain that names the operation each hop invokes (`orders#createOrder`, then `payment#charge`), with the proof for that route. boundaryInfluence is the influence an egress sends to another organisation: under the boundary `key`, for `rid`, the partner entry `rcv` and the `egress`, the `input` entries reduce to `reduced`, with one salt (base64url) per (cls, owner) group in `salts`; each `openings` case is a `sent` entry and an `opening`, with its JCS bytes in `body` (hex), which the replay reads, and `opens` says whether it opens. `operations` holds `table`, an operation table as a `file` (its text) and `value`, with its `opsHash` and the `route` a root covers it as; `shared`, payment's table, an entrance with two operations told apart by a query condition, in the same form; `keyed`, a table whose operations declare keys, in the same form; `refused`, table files a reader refuses; `match`, a method, a raw path and a raw query (null for none) against a table `file` and the operation name it gives, null for none; `keys`, cases giving a call's operation in `keyed` and its key value, null for none; and `receive`, a request entered at `orders` through the HTTP receiver under enforce, on the `ops` policy, against a nonce cache that already holds `spent` (none when absent), whose chain's first stamp names `orders` or an operation of it, its `X-Path-Extensions` one empty block per stamp, with the `operation` the framework dispatches to (null for none), the receiver's `actsOn` and `allowedExtensions` as above, and the `refusal` it expects (null when the request is served). Every `receive` case carries the proof of `gateway/orders#createOrder`, whatever its chain names. Ed25519 is deterministic, so the file is reproduced byte for byte. Java writes and replays this file; Go replays http-v3.json until it moves; the TypeScript SDK has no HTTP binding, so it does not replay it.
